findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, Second Reading (House vote 66-47, he voted Aye)
findings.note: Voted aye on House second reading of HB 958, a bill making various election law changes. The ratified text includes a requirement that a voter registration application affirmatively state US citizenship before it is processed (with a 30-day notice and penalty-of-perjury form if blank), and a process for removing registrants flagged as possible non-citizens in a federal database. Voter ID at the polls is not in the passages checked.

findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, M11 Concur (House vote 62-47, he voted Aye)
findings.note: Voted aye to concur with the Senate changes to HB 958. The bill page shows it was then vetoed by the Governor on 08/17/2026; the outcome of any override was not found on the pages fetched.

findings.motion: HB 958 ratified text, Section 2.4(c), new G.S. 163-83
findings.note: Bill text he voted for. Passage: "When making the tentative determination of qualification in accordance with G.S. 163-82.7(a), the county board shall process the voter registration application in accordance with this Article only if the voter registration application affirmatively indicates that the applicant is a citizen of the United States." This is bill text, not his own words. Date given is the date of the concur vote.

findings.motion: Second Reading, Election Law Changes (66 Ayes, 47 Noes)
findings.note: Member vote list shows Aye on Second Reading, Election Law Changes. The ratified text of HB 958 adds a rule that a county board processes a registration application only if the applicant affirmatively says they are a U.S. citizen, with a sworn citizenship form for blank answers, and orders a process to remove voters flagged as non-citizens by a federal database. The bill page shows the Governor vetoed it on 2026-08-17.
